[!WARNING]
 OpenLogi is under active development and not yet stable — features and config may still change. Give the repo a Star ⭐ and Watch 👀 it to get notified when a new release lands.

 
 
 

 OpenLogi 
 ⚡️ A native, local-first alternative to Logitech Options+, written in Rust 🦀 Unlock the full capabilities of Logitech mice, keyboards, and webcams over HID++ and UVC 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 Fed up with Options+? Try OpenLogi. 

Runs on macOS, Linux, and Windows.

---

 Beyond Options+

Things OpenLogi does that Options+ won't:

- Stay light. Native Rust + GPUI.
- Run on Linux. Linux is a first-class platform in OpenLogi.
- Gestures on supported buttons. Assign gesture actions to supported controls — or turn gestures off entirely.
- Plain-text config. Everything is one TOML file you can sync between machines however you like.
- Script it. A real CLI alongside the GUI: a JSON automation API for DPI, SmartShift, Fn-lock, and report rate, plus hardware diagnostics.

 Features

 
 
 

 Devices

- Logi Bolt and Unifying receivers, Bluetooth, and wired connections, with battery level and charge state
- Low-battery notices at the bottom of the screen, once per discharge, with no OS notification permission
- An on-screen indicator when a keyboard turns Caps Lock on or off, plus Num Lock and Scroll Lock on Windows and Linux
- On macOS, a menu-bar menu that lists each device with its battery or light state, flags a missing permission, and changes the settings you reach for most without opening the app: DPI preset, wheel mode, Fn lock, backlight, disabled keys, headset sidetone, and a light's power, brightness, and color temperature. Hold ⌥ to see how each device connects

 
 
 
 Easy-Switch See which computer is paired on each channel, with its OS and connection Rename a channel on devices that allow it Bind a button or Actions Ring slot to move the device to another channel 
 
 

 Buttons and actions

 
 
 
 Remap any button A built-in action catalog, custom shortcuts, typed text, or multi-step workflows Separate tap and hold actions, and hold-to-talk chords that release with the button Gestures on Middle Click, Back/Forward, DPI/ModeShift, the gesture button, and the haptic panel 
 
 
 
 Actions Ring Eight actions in a ring around the cursor Its own layout per application 
 
 
 
 Keyboard keys Bind media, emoji, screenshot, and other dedicated keys like mouse buttons Restore one key to its device default, or reset the whole row 
 
 

Per-application profiles switch with the focused app. An [apps] alias lets one profile follow an application across platforms.

 Pointer and scrolling

 
 
 
 Pointer DPI presets with cycle and set-preset actions Pointer speed and report rate Precision Mode: one button switches the mouse to its slowest speed and back 
 
 
 
 SmartShift Wheel mode and sensitivity Scrolling force on SmartShift Enhanced mice A permanent-ratchet switch 
 
 
 Scrolling Scroll inversion per device, natively or in software Wheel resolution and smooth wheel scrolling Hold Back or Forward and roll the wheel to scroll sideways on mice without a thumb wheel 
 
 

 Keyboard and lighting

 
 
 
 Keyboard Fn Lock, and multi-platform keyboards that stay on the host OS layout Backlight level, automatic brightness, battery saving, and how long the keys stay lit The backlight level shown on screen as it changes Static RGB on supported keyboards 
 
 
 
 Litra lights Power, brightness, and color temperature Turns on with the camera if you want Keeps a change made on the light itself 
 
 

 Webcams

- Any Logitech UVC webcam (Brio, StreamCam, the C920 series, …), plug and play
- Live preview that holds the camera only while you watch; leave it and the LED goes off
- Pick the preview's resolution and frame rate from the modes your camera reports (this shapes OpenLogi's own preview, not what other apps get)
- On macOS and Windows, a camera on a slower USB link than it supports (a USB 2 port, hub, or cable) is flagged, since it lists fewer resolutions and frame rates than it can deliver on USB 3
- Zoom, pan, tilt, focus, exposure, white balance, and every other UVC control, written to the hardware so Meet, Zoom, and OBS see the change
- Built-in Default / Streaming / Video call profiles plus your own snapshots, kept per camera

Feature coverage depends on what each device reports; the app shows only the controls a device supports.

 Platform support

 Feature macOS Windows Linux 
 --- --- --- --- 
 Mouse button remapping and gestures ✓ ✓ ✓ 
 Keyboard F-key remapping ✓ ✓ — 
 Per-application profiles ✓ ✓ X11, wlroots (sway, Hyprland), GNOME with the companion extension 
 Mouse profile follows the window under the pointer ✓ ✓ X11 only 
 Media keys Native Native D-Bus MPRIS 
 Window-manager actions (desktops, Mission Control, …) Native Native equivalents GNOME, KDE (KWin), Hyprland; some macOS-only actions do nothing 
 Menu-bar / tray icon ✓ ✓ — 
 Device controls in the menu-bar / tray menu ✓ — — 
 In-app updates Sparkle Built-in Built-in 

 Install

 [!IMPORTANT]
 Quit Logi Options+ (and Solaar on Linux) first. Only one application can own a receiver at a time.
 On macOS, Karabiner-Elements also locks a Bluetooth keyboard that it modifies. Turn off Modify events for that keyboard in Karabiner-Elements → Settings → Devices.

 Platform System Architecture 
 --- --- --- 
 macOS macOS 13 or later Apple silicon, Intel 
 Linux GLIBC 2.35 or newer x86 64, arm64 
 Windows Tested on Windows 11 x86 64, arm64

install.title: Install
install.html:
[!IMPORTANT] Quit Logi Options+ (and Solaar on Linux) first. Only one application can own a receiver at a time. On macOS, Karabiner-Elements also locks a Bluetooth keyboard that it modifies. Turn off Modify events for that keyboard in Karabiner-Elements → Settings → Devices.

Platform System Architecture
macOS macOS 13 or later Apple silicon, Intel
Linux GLIBC 2.35 or newer x86_64, arm64
Windows Tested on Windows 11 x86_64, arm64

Every download carries a minisign signature and an entry in SHA256SUMS. To build from source, see DEVELOPMENT.md.

macOS

 

Or with Homebrew:

brew install --cask openlogi

Open OpenLogi and grant Accessibility and Input Monitoring when macOS asks. OpenLogi then updates itself through Sparkle.

Linux

   

Or install the right package for your distribution with one command. It verifies the minisign signature and starts the agent; install minisign first:

curl -fsSL https://github.com/AprilNEA/OpenLogi/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh

On Arch Linux, the openlogi AUR package builds the release from source:

yay -S openlogi

To read the script before running it, and for the AUR package, Flatpak, NixOS, and distributions without systemd, see INSTALL-linux.md.
